transcript.text: Hi, I got your email. What should I do first? I haven't set up any boards yet.

Welcome! The best place to start is your **first board**. None of the four setup steps are done yet, and the board comes first.

**To create your first board:**
1. Click **New board** on the home page.
2. Pick a template:
   - **Kanban**: a simple to-do, doing, done flow
   - **Sprint**: for teams that work in iterations
   - **Roadmap**: for planning by quarter
   - **Project plan**: for work with dates and owners
3. Add a few real cards. Give each one an owner and a due date.
4. Click **Share** to share the board with your team.

A board with real work on it is the quickest way to get your colleagues using Relay.

**After that, the next steps are:**
2. **Invite at least five people.** You have 4 of your 15 seats assigned so far.
3. **Connect an integration.** Chat or calendar are the easiest to start with.
4. **Set up single sign-on (SSO).** Your Standard edition includes it.

You can check your progress anytime under **Admin settings → Setup progress**. Do you want help choosing a template or with any of the next steps?

transcript.text: How do I invite my whole team at once? There are about a dozen of us.

For about 12 people, pasting the addresses is quickest:

1. Go to **Admin settings → Users → Invite**.
2. Type or paste the email addresses, one per line.
3. Send. Each person gets an email with a link that works for 7 days.

**Uploading a file:** If you'd rather use a file, choose **Upload a file** on the same Invite screen. Upload a CSV with a column named `email`. You can add a `role` column set to `member` or `admin`. Relay checks the file first and lists any addresses it can't use, such as a typo or someone who's already a user. Nothing is sent until you confirm.

**Check your seats:** Your plan has 15 seats and 4 are already in use, so you have **11 free**. An invitation takes up a seat as soon as it's sent. If 12 new people need invitations, you'll be one seat short. You can free a seat by cancelling a pending invitation or deactivating an unused user. If you need more seats, I can connect you with someone about your plan.

**If invitations don't arrive:** Ask people to check their spam folder. If your company filters outside email, ask IT to allow mail from `relay-mail.lumenlabs.example`.

Inviting your team also finishes the "invite at least five users" setup step. You still have two steps left: connecting an integration and setting up single sign-on.
How do I connect our calendar so due dates show up there?

Here's how to connect your calendar:

1. Go to **Admin settings → Integrations → Calendar** and click **Connect**. Only admins can do this.
2. Approve access in your calendar tool. You'll then be sent back to Relay, and the integration is on for the whole workspace right away.

After that, any card with **both a due date and an assignee** shows up in that person's calendar.

**If due dates don't appear:**
- Make sure the card has both a due date and an assignee.
- Make sure the assignee has accepted the calendar permission request. Each person gets it by email.
- Make sure the board isn't archived.
- Wait a bit. New or changed dates can take up to 15 minutes to show up.

Connecting this also completes one of your remaining setup steps. After that, the only step left is single sign-on.
Where do I set up single sign-on? Our IT team is asking.

Your account is on the Standard edition, so single sign-on (SSO) is included. It's also the last setup step you have left.

**Where to find it:** go to **Admin settings → Security → Single sign-on**. Only admins can change these settings.

**Steps for your IT team:**
1. Choose the protocol your identity provider uses: **SAML** or **OIDC**.
2. Enter the provider's details:
   - **SAML:** upload the identity provider's metadata file (XML).
   - **OIDC:** paste the client ID, client secret and issuer URL.
3. Click **Test connection**. Relay will sign you in through your provider in a new window.
4. If the test works, click **Enable for everyone**.

Keep one admin account that signs in with a password until you've confirmed SSO works for the whole team, so you can't get locked out. Setup usually takes 10–15 minutes.
My colleagues say the invitation emails never arrived. What can I check?

Check these, in this order:

1. **Spam or junk folder.** Ask your colleagues to look there first.
2. **The email addresses.** Go to **Admin settings → Users → Pending invitations** and check each address. A typo is the most common cause.
3. **Resend.** Click **Resend** next to the invitation. The old link will stop working, so tell them to use the new email.
4. **Company email filtering.** If your company blocks external email, ask your IT team to allow mail from **relay-mail.lumenlabs.example**.

Invitations expire after seven days. An expired invitation still takes up a seat until you resend or cancel it. You have 4 of your 15 seats assigned, so you have plenty free if you need to invite anyone again.
How do automation rules work with recurring cards?

Automation rules work with recurring cards. Each time Relay creates a new copy of a recurring card, the rule runs on that copy.

**Setting up a rule:** On any board, click the **Automation** button. Pick a trigger, add conditions if you want them, and choose one or more actions. For example: when a card moves to Done, notify the reporter.

**Rule limits by edition:** Free allows 5 rules per workspace, Standard 15, Premium 60, and Enterprise has no practical limit. If you hit the limit, your current rules keep running, but you can't add new ones.

**If a rule doesn't run or runs twice:** Open the Automation panel on the board and look at the rule's run history.
- **It didn't run:** the rule may be switched off, the trigger may be set on a different list, or a condition (like a label or assignee) may not have matched.
- **It runs twice:** two rules probably have the same trigger. The copy may be on the board or in the workspace template the board came from. Switch one of them off.
Can someone outside our company see just one board, as a guest?

Yes. You're on the Standard edition, which includes guest access.

**To invite a guest:**
1. Open the board you want to share.
2. Click **Share**.
3. Type their email address and choose **Guest**.

**What a guest can see:** Only the boards you invite them to. They can't see other boards or your list of users.

**Seats:** Guests don't take up one of your licensed seats.

**To remove a guest later:** Remove them in **Share** on that board, or deactivate them under **Admin settings → Users → Guests**.
How do I deactivate a user who left, so they stop using a seat?

To deactivate someone who left:

1. Go to **Admin settings → Users**.
2. Find the person, open the **menu at the end of their row**, and choose **Deactivate**.

What happens next:
- **The seat is freed right away**, so you can give it to someone else.
- **Their cards, comments and documents stay where they are.** Any cards assigned to them will show as unassigned, so you may want to give those to someone else.
- **You can undo this.** If you reactivate them later, they get their history back.

If you want to delete the user permanently instead, only support can do that, because it can't be undone. For freeing a seat, deactivating is enough.
Which setup steps are we still missing on the checklist?

You've finished 2 of the 4 setup steps: you created your first board and invited at least five people (you have 9 of 15 seats assigned). Two steps are left:

**1. Connect an integration**
- Go to **Admin settings → Integrations**, pick a tool and click **Connect**. You'll approve access in that tool, then come back to Relay.
- It goes live right away for the whole workspace.
- Your Standard edition lets you connect up to 3. The choices are chat, calendar, code repository, cloud drive, CRM and video meetings. Chat or calendar are the fastest to get value from.

3. Click **Test connection**. If the test works, click **Enable for everyone**.
4. Keep one admin account that signs in with a password until you've confirmed SSO works for everyone.

Automation rules work on recurring cards. **Each time a new copy of the card is created, the rule runs on it.**

You're on the Standard edition, so your workspace can have up to 15 rules. If you reach that limit, your existing rules keep running, but you can't add new ones.
